resources.string: Apps only filters user or system apps without changing the saved order. Selecting an app prioritizes it in supported candidate menus, not as the Android default. Long-press an app row for the three-dot menu; drag the right-hand handle to reorder. Unlock a locked row before selecting it; bulk actions skip locked entries. Confirm Apply changes at the bottom to save.

Long-press and move the right-hand drag handle to reorder a prioritized app. Releasing it only updates the pending order; confirm Apply changes at the bottom to save. Long-press the app row for the three-dot menu. Expanded apps also support Move up and Move down. Edit a component menu label through its three-dot menu; save an empty label to restore the original.
Current ordering source: inherited from Open · All

Neither this type nor All has priority ordering

A type without a dedicated order inherits All. The first select, deselect, drag or move action creates a pending dedicated order based on that inherited order; confirm Apply changes to save it. Restoring inheritance resumes following changes to All. Built-in and custom types behave the same way.

Priority ordering and display names are saved per entry category. Only supported categories allow ordering; vendor pickers may reorder candidates again. DocumentsUI storage roots and Settings screen savers use best-effort hooks. This does not change Android Roles, default apps, service enablement, permissions, app names, component names, or targets.
